claims.text: A high NaBH4 concentration produces rapid reduction of the noble-metal precursors.
Rapid reduction synchronizes nucleation of all metal species.
Synchronized nucleation locks the metals into a homogeneous, single-phase noble-metal high-entropy alloy.
The rapidly reduced alloy has uniformly dispersed catalytic active sites.
The homogeneous single-phase structure enhances catalytic performance relative to material made under slower reduction conditions.
Slow reduction permits kinetic segregation and phase separation.
Increasing NaBH4 concentration while holding the other reaction conditions constant modulates the precursor reduction rate.
Rapidly reduced nanoparticles form uniform local atomic-scale ordering and coherent lattice distortions.
High configurational entropy maintains the local ordering and coherent lattice distortions in the rapidly reduced nanoparticles.
Slow reduction gives the metal species enough time to develop compositional inhomogeneity.
Relative to the slow-reduction baseline, the rapid-reduction sample will exhibit a single phase and coherent lattice distortions by XRD and high-resolution STEM.
Relative to the slow-reduction baseline, the rapid-reduction sample will exhibit improved turnover frequency and a lower catalytic onset potential.
The slow-reduction sample will exhibit elemental segregation and lower catalytic activity.
The proposed relationship is expected to apply near 25°C under an inert atmosphere when NaBH4-controlled reduction kinetics is the primary variable affecting nanoparticle nucleation and growth.
Synthesis parameters other than reduction kinetics and thermodynamic factors may also influence atomic mixing.
